ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, trolley A is on the horizontal plane on the left side, and the arrow marked with speed v points to the left; a rope goes from the connection point above trolley A obliquely upward to the right, reaches the fixed pulley at the upper right, passes around the pulley, and then vertically downward suspends object B. The pulley is fixed on the upper bracket, and B is at the lower end of the vertical rope segment on the right side. Then reason: Let the length of the oblique rope segment from A to the pulley be l, the horizontal projection of the oblique rope segment be x, and the vertical projection be h. Since trolley A moves on the horizontal plane and the pulley is fixed, h is unchanged, l=sqrt(x^2+h^2). When A moves to the left with constant speed v, x increases at a constant speed, therefore dl/dt=vx/l. As x increases, x/l also increases, so dl/dt increases; the oblique rope segment not only becomes longer but also the speed of becoming longer increases, that is d²l/dt²>0. The total length of the rope is unchanged, therefore the length of the vertical rope segment on the right side correspondingly decreases, and the decreasing speed increases, indicating that B moves upward and has an upward acceleration. For the force analysis of B, B is subject to the upward tension T and the downward gravitational force mg. Taking upward as positive, from Newton's second law we get T-mg=ma. Because the acceleration a of B is upward and a>0, T-mg>0, that is T>mg.
